newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey prepares "warning" to Moody's on report.
newsitem.headline: Turkey prepares "warning" to Moody's on report.

text.p: Turkey's Treasury is preparing a warning to U.S. credit rating agency Moody's in response to its recent report of a deteriorating financial situation at Turkish banks, state-run Anatolian news agency said on Tuesday.

It quoted State Minister Ufuk Soylemez, in charge of the Treasury, saying in Washington that "the Treasury is preparing a warning letter on my instructions, asking them the reasons for such an unauthorised report."
"(It) will tell them with numerical detail and one by one all the mistakes and missing points in the report about the Turkish banking sector."

"The Turkish banking sector is much more qualified than other Western banks in many respects," the agency quoted him as saying on the sidelines of an interim meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

"It would be greatly unfair to our banking system to give serious consideration to a news item carrying a Moody's report prepared in Limassol (Cyprus) lacking a clear purpose and evaluating Turkish banks negatively," he said.
Moody's said in its report published last week in Limassol that the Turkish banking sector was constrained by the country's "persistent macroeconomic and political instability".
It blamed Turkey's economic woes on a high fiscal deficit, inefficient public enterprises, a bankrupt social security system and a narrow tax base.
Soylemez said the report was "a real scandal on the part of Moody's and nothing but a remote control."
He said the Treasury's reply letter will be disclosed to the public when it is ready.
